slot.brief: Given three ions, ask which has the maximum number of unpaired electrons with a brief reason via electronic configuration.

stem: Among the following ions, the one with the maximum number of unpaired electrons is:

verdicts.working: Mn²⁺ is [Ar]3d⁵, with 5 unpaired electrons; Fe²⁺, Co²⁺, and Ni²⁺ have 4, 3, and 2, respectively.

working:
Electronic configurations of the high-spin aquated ions: Mn$^{2+}$: [Ar]3d$^5$ → 5 unpaired electrons; Fe$^{2+}$: [Ar]3d$^6$ → 4 unpaired; Co$^{2+}$: [Ar]3d$^7$ → 3 unpaired; Ni$^{2+}$: [Ar]3d$^8$ → 2 unpaired. Hence Mn$^{2+}$ has the greatest number of unpaired electrons.

Independent check: Mn²⁺ is [Ar]3d⁵, with 5 unpaired electrons; Fe²⁺, Co²⁺, and Ni²⁺ have 4, 3, and 2, respectively.
solution: For high-spin ions, remove the $4s$ electrons first: $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}=[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^5$, with one electron in each of the five $d$ orbitals. It has $5$ unpaired electrons, more than $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ ($4$), $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$ ($3$), or $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ ($2$).
